source_refs.note: Topic 2.8.1.4 Association (PDF 59, printed 56). The printed code has 'self, books' for self.books and a duplicated print line.

blocks.text: Association represents a relationship between two classes. There are two types of association:

items: Aggregation: Represents a relationship where one class (e.g., Library) contains another class (e.g., Book) but does not own it. Books can exist independently of the library.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: As printed this code does not work: self, books = [ ] should be self.books = [ ] (the comma makes a ValueError); def add_book must be indented inside class Library, with its two lines indented under it (the print line is over-indented); and the string "added to the library.” ends with a curly quote, so it is never closed. Corrected, lib.add_book(Book("...")) prints Book  ... added to the library.
Explanation: The above code made association by passing an instance of the 'Book' class to the 'Library' class through the 'add_book' method, which appends the book to the library's list of books.
Composition: Represents a relationship where one class (e.g., House) contains and owns another class (e.g.. Room). Rooms cannot exist without a house.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: self.name = name is printed at the margin; it must be indented inside __init__ (IndentationError). The print inside House uses curly quotes (“House with rooms created”), which Python does not accept; use straight quotes. The last line, print("House with rooms created."), is an extra copy outside the class. The house is made with house = House(), which prints House with rooms created.

Explanation: The code demonstrates composition by creating a 'House' object that contains a list of 'Rooms' objects, each representing a room (like 'Living Room' and 'Bedroom'). The 'House' class depends on the 'Room' class to define its components.
